Dear Kranich team,

Kranich builds the kind of logistics software I already work next to: I have two years of professional experience with Node.js and TypeScript at Tessellate Labs, where I maintain the invoicing service for our logistics clients, which issues about 9,000 invoices a month.

I cut the nightly reconciliation job from 41 minutes to 6 by replacing row-by-row updates with set-based SQL and adding two partial indexes. I also moved four services to Docker Compose.

I have no experience with SAP, DATEV or RabbitMQ. When nobody at work knew Docker Compose, I learned it in time for a two-week migration.

Could we arrange a short call?

Best regards,
Rania Haroon

Dear Kranich team,

The billing team at Tessellate is four people and a shared Google Doc called 'things that scared us this week'. Anyone can add to it, and on Fridays we go through it together. Half the items are nothing. The other half turn into tickets before they turn into incidents. A team that already holds an architecture round every fortnight probably knows the feeling.

I build Node.js and TypeScript services on PostgreSQL. I maintain an invoicing service for logistics clients, about 9,000 invoices a month, and I cut our reconciliation job from 41 minutes to 6 with set-based SQL and two partial indexes.

My tables have been far smaller than yours, and your partitioning post is where I'd start.

Could we arrange a short call?

Best regards,
Rania Haroon
